hypothesis_status: Retrospective explanation of completed analyses; not a claim of preregistration. New checks are separately specified before execution.

papers.author: Mikkel Plagborg-Møller and Christian K. Wolf
papers.title: Local Projections and VARs Estimate the Same Impulse Responses
papers.application: LP and VAR can target the same population response. Agreement is not independent causal identification; finite lag choices matter.

papers.author: José Luis Montiel Olea and Mikkel Plagborg-Møller
papers.title: Local Projection Inference Is Simpler and More Robust Than You Think
papers.application: Lag-augmented LP inference needs its own conditions. The published baseline HAC/VAR-bootstrap implementation is not automatically this procedure.

papers.author: Dake Li and Mikkel Plagborg-Møller and Christian K. Wolf
papers.title: Local Projections vs. VARs: Lessons from Thousands of DGPs
papers.application: Compare finite-sample bias, variance and coverage across several data-generating processes, rather than treating LP as universally superior.

papers.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant’Anna
papers.title: Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods
papers.application: Use cohort-time treatment effects and eligible comparisons when opening dates differ. This is the primary municipal design, not an estimated result yet.

papers.author: Pedro H. C. Sant’Anna and Jun Zhao
papers.title: Doubly Robust Difference-in-Differences Estimators
papers.application: Doubly robust means consistency if one of two nuisance models is correct under the design assumptions. It does not remove unobserved confounding or guarantee inference.

papers.author: Liyang Sun and Sarah Abraham
papers.title: Estimating Dynamic Treatment Effects in Event Studies with Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
papers.application: Avoid a naive common-effect, two-way fixed-effects event study: heterogeneous effects can contaminate leads and lags.

papers.author: Jonathan Roth
papers.title: Pretest with Caution: Event-Study Estimates after Testing for Parallel Trends
papers.application: A non-significant pretrend can reflect low power. Do not select the reported specification because it passes a pretest.

papers.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth
papers.title: A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends
papers.application: Assess how conclusions change under bounded departures from parallel trends. A validated Python sensitivity implementation remains pending.

papers.author: Bradley Setzler and Felix Tintelnot
papers.title: The Effects of Foreign Multinationals on Workers and Firms in the United States
papers.scope: multinational investment application; not Brazil estimates
papers.application: US worker–firm evidence motivates direct and indirect channels. Its estimates are not Brazilian effects or a calibration for our municipalities.

papers.author: Alonso Alfaro-Ureña and Isabela Manelici and Jose P. Vasquez
papers.title: The Effects of Joining Multinational Supply Chains: New Evidence from Firm-to-Firm Linkages
papers.scope: multinational investment application; not Brazil estimates
papers.application: Costa Rican supplier-link evidence motivates supply-chain mechanisms. Evaluate its identification separately; do not transplant its coefficients or comparison design.

books.title: The Book of Why: The New Science of Cause and Effect
books.sections: Chapter 1 (PDF pp. 34–37); Chapter 4 (PDF pp. 143, 148–152). PDF pagination refers to the inspected reflowed copy, not print pages.
books.application: Distinguish seeing from doing and counterfactual questions. Draw common causes, mediators and colliders before choosing controls. The diagram expresses assumptions; it does not verify them.

books.title: Statistical Models: Theory and Practice
books.sections: Chapter 1, pp. 1–14; Chapter 6, pp. 81–87; Chapter 8, pp. 155–156.
books.application: Ask whether a fitted relationship would remain stable under an intervention. Report the economic size of a one-standard-deviation shock. Distinguish 2,000 simulated bootstrap draws from 119 observed quarters.

books.title: A Guide to Modern Econometrics
books.sections: Section 2.5.7, pp. 30–31; Section 5.2.4, p. 148; Section 9.2, p. 363.
books.application: Explain p-values and power, reverse causality and the predictive meaning of Granger tests. A small p-value or an ability to predict does not itself establish an intervention effect.

supersession.frozen_specification: The original study archive is preserved. Its unexecuted R municipal plan and unrecovered-poster wording are historical metadata, not the active implementation or current evidence.
supersession.legacy_eligibility_flag: The frozen national causal_release_eligible flag records the original diagnostic gate, not certification of economic identification. The active public claim remains conditional on explicit restrictions.
supersession.publication_policy: The frozen original release-policy wording is historical. The available-data website is authorized for release; the LinkedIn article remains an unpublished draft.
supersession.active_municipal: Python ModernDiD 0.4.0 / Callaway–Sant’Anna doubly robust design; no empirical municipal ATT has been estimated.
supersession.poster: The original PUC-SP poster is recovered. The original underlying data, code and full manuscripts remain unrecovered.
supersession.fevd: The reviewed public FEVD already uses responses 0 through h−1 for an h-quarter forecast. The native archive summary is retained unchanged; do not export it directly as the reviewed series.
supersession.robustness: Additional Python robustness notebook is prepared, not a completed sensitivity or Monte Carlo study.
